reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is a rare-event detection duality: DPI occurs when defenders and attackers occupy the same 3D space near the ball, yet GPS data lacks direct line-of-sight measurements. The authors employ LSTM-FCN fusion to map high-dimensional spatio-temporal trajectories onto binary outcomes. However, the resulting models exhibit high recall (detecting true positives) but low precision (many false alarms). This failure mode arises because the training data overwhelmingly consists of non-interference frames; the model learns to predict the majority class, leading to systematic over-prediction of interference. To address this, GSI can deploy conformal prediction to generate well-calibrated p-values for each DPI call, while GSE can use the LSTM embeddings as priors for sequential hypothesis testing on replay video.
